why: One rule, two implementations: src/model/coverage.rs (recipe_cover, share) and src/db/foods.rs (recipe_per100) own it; web/coverage.mjs (recipeKnown, recipePer100, coverage) mirrors it for the editor's live panel. cargo and node both read this file. A part is {per100, grams, drink?, known?, borne?}; with no water value and not a drink, all its grams are dry matter. Expected values are worked out by hand in each `why`.

recipes.name: spice
recipes.why: Oats 50 g, milk 200 g, spice 50 g, all dry: 300 g of dry matter over 300 g is 100 per 100 g. Energy is on oats and milk (250 of 300), iron on oats (50 of 300), protein on the spice (50 of 300).

recipes.name: cooked
recipes.why: Oats (90 g dry a 100 g) and milk (10 g dry) 100 g each, cooked to 150 g: 100 g of dry matter over 150 g is 66.67 per 100 g; iron is on the oats' 90 of it. Cooking takes 50 g of water: 100 - 50 = 50 g in 150 g.

recipes.name: subDry
recipes.why: A sub-recipe of 10 g dry a 100 g whose iron is half known, and a dry food, 100 g each: (10 + 100) / 2 = 55 dry; iron is behind half of the sub-recipe's 10, 2.5 of 55. Mutant C8 (the sub-recipe's own dry ignored) reads 0.25.

recipes.name: juice
recipes.why: A juice (a drink without a water value: 100 - 10 - 1 = 89 g water, 11 g dry) 200 g, and bread (40 g water, 60 g dry) 100 g: (22 + 60) / 3 = 27.33 dry. Fibre and iron are the juice's 7.33 of it, water the bread's 20. Mutant C11 (the drink flag ignored) counts the juice as all dry.

recipes.name: coffee
recipes.why: Two coffees of 200 g (2 g dry a 100 g), both able to hold caffeine (borne 100), one saying how much: caffeine is weighed by what could hold it, half of it known. Dry matter is 2 a 100 g.

recipes.name: allWater
recipes.why: Only water: no dry matter, so nothing can be unknown and no key is listed. Mutant C9 (a share of nothing as 0) lists water and iron as unknown.

shares.why: A key `known` lists is its share.
A key of the total `known` doesn't list is known in full.
A key the total lacks is not known at all.
A borne key the total lacks: nothing that could hold it was eaten, a known none.
